nodes.label: IMPORTANT: This runs entirely client-side via the Firestore SDK.
nodes.norm_label: important: this runs entirely client-side via the firestore sdk.

nodes.label: Exception Review Workflow and Open-Session Monitor
nodes.norm_label: exception review workflow and open-session monitor
nodes.rationale: Implausibly long sessions, sessions reopened after a missed check-out, and sessions split by a back-dated roster change raise a review item moving flagged -> in review -> resolved. A scheduled job runs every fifteen minutes and only ever raises a review - it never closes a session or truncates recorded hours.

nodes.label: Fingerprint and Mobile Capture in One Record
nodes.norm_label: fingerprint and mobile capture in one record
nodes.rationale: Terminal punches are written into the same attendance sessions the mobile application uses so they appear immediately in every existing report with no separate reconciliation; each punch shows its own source badge for check-in and check-out independently.

nodes.label: Terminal Integration Safeguards
nodes.rationale: Idempotent per scan, debounced against duplicate punches, device and employee validated, coded errors returned; a rejected scan is not locked in so an offline terminal's retry queue still succeeds once the underlying issue is fixed.

nodes.label: Raw Punches Are Never Rewritten
nodes.rationale: Original timestamps are preserved exactly as captured and interpretation lives in a separate layer that allocates a session into rostered and unverified-extra time, so the audit trail of what the terminal actually recorded stays intact.

nodes.label: Register Scope and Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Payroll is implemented for Southern Lanka but excluded by request and summarised separately; leave management appears only where it touches HOD routing and roster overlays; the Suspense module is built but switched off for this tenant; working patterns are designed but not yet built and tracked as planned work.

nodes.label: Bulk Roster Import with Review Step
nodes.norm_label: bulk roster import with review step
nodes.rationale: Shift names are matched case-insensitively against the department's registered shifts; anything unrecognised is flagged rather than guessed, and nothing is written until the reviewer confirms.

nodes.label: Holiday Classification Stamped at Assignment
nodes.rationale: Poya, Public and Mercantile classification is stamped onto the assignment when it is made so that editing the holiday list later never retroactively changes what a past roster recorded.

nodes.label: Module 01 - Tenant and Multi-Company Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Employee-to-hierarchy mapping is a single mapping that drives every downstream scope: who appears on a roster, whose attendance a manager can open, and where a leave request is routed. Department deletion is a recoverable soft delete, never a permanent erase.

nodes.label: Module 02 - Users and Role-Based Access
nodes.rationale: Roles are configuration, not code: administrators create job titles, tick capabilities and place the role in the approval hierarchy from inside the application with no release required.

nodes.label: Module 03 - HOD Scope and Reporting Lines
nodes.norm_label: module 03 - hod scope and reporting lines
nodes.rationale: Head of Department is a role, but the departments a person heads are assigned individually; that assignment is the boundary for everything a HOD can see and approve and it is enforced when data is loaded, not merely hidden in the interface.

nodes.label: Module 04 - Shift Definition and Scheduling Engine
nodes.norm_label: module 04 - shift definition and scheduling engine
nodes.rationale: Shifts are defined once and reused across departments; rostering is a calendar grid of employees against dates supporting split days, back-to-back duty, midnight-crossing shifts, recurring weekly patterns and bulk spreadsheet import.

nodes.label: Module 05 - Attendance and Real-Time Roster Engine
nodes.norm_label: module 05 - attendance and real-time roster engine
nodes.rationale: A monthly attendance matrix scored against each employee's actual rostered shifts rather than a fixed clock-in cutoff; anything implausible is flagged for a supervisor rather than silently corrected.

nodes.label: Recurring Weekly Roster Patterns
nodes.rationale: A pattern writes ordinary roster entries on a rolling horizon, extended weekly by a scheduled job, so every existing view and report reads it unchanged. The engine only ever touches entries it created - a hand-placed shift on the same date is left alone.

nodes.label: Strict HOD Scope Resolution (no fallback)
nodes.rationale: A HOD role with no departments assigned resolves to no access - never to 'sees everything' - and the scope never falls back to the person's own home department, which is where they sit rather than what they manage. Employee lists, attendance records, roster assignments and stored monthly summaries are filtered as they load so out-of-scope staff are never held in the session at all.

nodes.label: Southern Lanka Capability Register
nodes.rationale: A consolidated production capability view for the Southern Lanka / CareCode tenant, compiled from the implemented application rather than from specification documents. Modules are listed in dependency order because each relies on the data and permissions established by the one above it.

nodes.label: Overnight Shift Handling (end <= start crosses midnight)
nodes.norm_label: overnight shift handling (end <= start crosses midnight)
nodes.rationale: Treated consistently across assignment, overlap detection, hour totals and attendance scoring, and labelled with a next-day marker so it is never misread as an earlier same-day time.

nodes.label: Recalculation on Retrospective Roster Change
nodes.rationale: Back-dating, editing or removing a roster entry queues a recalculation for that employee and date range so attendance interpretation stays consistent with the roster it is scored against.

nodes.label: Domain-Resolved Data Isolation
nodes.rationale: The database is selected per request from the hostname, so no Southern Lanka record is readable from another tenant's domain and no rebuild or separate deployment is needed.

nodes.label: Per-Employee Attendance Method Policy
nodes.rationale: Each employee is explicitly permitted to mark attendance by fingerprint terminal, by mobile application, or both. Records predating the policy are shown as 'Not set' rather than silently assumed.

nodes.label: Granular 38-Switch Capability Model
nodes.rationale: Thirty-eight independent switches gate every page and action, with separate read-only capabilities beside manage capabilities so a role can be given visibility without edit rights. The System Administrator role implies every management capability so a newly added capability never has to be granted retroactively and an administrator can never be locked out by an incomplete role registry.

nodes.label: Cross-Tenant Administrator Mirroring
nodes.rationale: Active super administrators are mirrored into every tenant database so they can sign in and administer any organisation, with safeguards preventing a mirrored account from overwriting a real employee record.

nodes.label: Role-Tree Approval Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Each role names its parent; ancestors, descendants and peer lines are resolved from that tree to decide who may approve whom, with cycle protection when a role is re-parented.

nodes.label: Contiguous Duty Merging and Split-Day Separation
nodes.norm_label: contiguous duty merging and split-day separation
nodes.rationale: Same-day shifts that meet with a zero-minute gap merge into one duty block anchored at the first start and last end, so a missing punch between back-to-back shifts is never counted as a late arrival or early departure. Shifts with a real gap stay separate blocks scored on their own, and the gap is never counted as working time.

nodes.label: Leave and Overtime Approval Routing
nodes.rationale: A request fans out to every active Head of Department covering the applicant's department plus every approving tier above them in the role tree. A HOD is never an approver of their own request - it escalates upward instead. Attendance corrections route to the covering HOD, falling back to the nearest approving tier rather than broadcasting to every approver.

nodes.label: Shortfall Calculation Against the Roster
nodes.rationale: Late minutes run from the block's scheduled start to the actual check-in and early departure from the actual check-out to the block's scheduled end; both floor at zero so arriving early or staying late never offsets a shortfall elsewhere. Monthly totals are persisted as a stable figure for HR - the screen reports and never deducts pay or leave on its own.

nodes.label: Server-Side Action Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: When `action` is omitted the backend infers direction from session state. An explicit CHECK_IN over an open session closes it at this punch's raw timestamp (never truncated to a scheduled time), flags both sessions and raises a review row. A CHECK_OUT with no open session is REJECTED so no phantom session is ever created; the event is logged but not locked in so a retry can still succeed.

nodes.label: attendance_reviews Queue (flagged/in_review/resolved)
nodes.rationale: Anything implausible - a reconciled double check-in, a session running 20h or more - is parked for a supervisor rather than silently corrected, and closed pending rather than auto-approved.

nodes.label: Fingerprint Sessions Are Auto-Approved
nodes.rationale: A fingerprint match already proves identity plus physical presence, so no supervisor approval step is inserted; *_approved_by is the sentinel 'FINGERPRINT' rather than a real epf.

nodes.label: 45-Second Punch Debounce
nodes.rationale: Backed by fingerprint_last_punch/{epf_number}, an Admin-SDK-only global duplicate-punch guard.

nodes.label: fingerprint_attendance_events Idempotency Lock
nodes.rationale: The ledger exists only as the idempotency lock keyed by attendanceEventId - it is not a reporting surface. A REJECTED event is deliberately not locked in so the same id can be retried after the underlying problem is fixed.

nodes.label: Scans Write Into the Same attendances sessions[]
nodes.norm_label: scans write into the same attendances sessions[]
nodes.rationale: Rather than a standalone attendanceEvents ledger, a scan lands in the same attendances/{epf}_{date}.sessions[] array the mobile check-in/out flow uses, so it shows up immediately in every existing report and export with no reconciliation step.

nodes.label: POST /api/fingerprint/attendance/bulk
nodes.rationale: Offline queue flush always responds 200 with one result per event so a bad event never fails the batch. Events are processed in deviceTimestamp order rather than array order or in parallel, so one person's scans toggle check-in/check-out correctly.

nodes.label: MODULE_ROUTES Route-to-Flag Map
nodes.rationale: The app shell refuses to render an off-module route, so a new page needs a flag, a MODULE_ROUTES entry and its sidebar gate - hiding a nav row is never on its own enough to keep anyone out of a page.

nodes.label: Platform Admin (platform_admins registry)
nodes.rationale: The only cross-tenant authority in the app, granted by email in the tenants registry database and verified server-side. The platform_admin custom claim is a presentation hint and never an authority.

nodes.label: firestore.rules Deploy Targets ((default) and test only)
nodes.norm_label: firestore.rules deploy targets ((default) and test only)
nodes.rationale: The southernlanka database is not a deploy target, so firestore.southernlanka.rules never ships from this repo - do not assume a new collection is readable there.

nodes.label: Tenancy Model (one deployment, many domains)
nodes.rationale: There is no tenant list in the codebase - tenants live in their own Firestore database and are edited at /platform, so features are switched per tenant through TenantFeatures rather than by checking tenant.id at a call site.

nodes.label: TenantFeatures Flags
nodes.rationale: One flag per page on top of the cross-cutting ones, so a page inside a subsystem needs both (e.g. /payroll-runs needs payroll AND payrollRuns).

nodes.label: src/lib/tenants.ts Purity Constraint
nodes.rationale: It takes the tenant list as an argument and must never import firebase, so both browser and server can use the same host-matching logic.

nodes.label: verifyPlatformCaller Server-Side Check
nodes.rationale: A role can never grant Platform Admin: roles are edited inside a tenant, so if ticking a box in one organisation could confer platform access, anyone who can edit roles there would own every other organisation in the deployment. Widening verifyPlatformCaller to consult a role, capability, claim or users doc breaks this.

nodes.label: Module Flags and Three Read Sites
nodes.norm_label: module flags and three read sites
nodes.rationale: MODULE_ROUTES is read by useSidebarNav (whether the nav row renders), the (pages) layout (whether the route renders at all, so a bookmark or typed URL cannot reach a module the tenant does not have) and the page's own guard. Hiding a sidebar row on its own keeps nobody out.

nodes.label: /platform Configuration Surface
nodes.rationale: Access is a separate tier from a tenant's own is_super_admin - running one organisation confers nothing here. PLATFORM_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL is always admitted and cannot be revoked so an empty admin list can never lock everyone out; the sidebar button comes from a custom claim to cost no request while the server re-checks the real list on every call.

nodes.label: Adding a Domain Runbook
nodes.rationale: Registering the domain is the last step and the only one done in the UI. dbId is immutable once registered because re-pointing a live domain at another organisation's database is the worst thing this system could do, so there is no code path that writes one.

nodes.label: Shift-Worker Yesterday Look-Back on Check-Out
nodes.rationale: If a user is is_shift_worker and has no open session today, a check-out scan checks yesterday's attendance doc for an open session before opening a new one - the same convention the working-status feed uses.

nodes.label: WORKFORCE_API_KEY Shared-Secret Auth
nodes.rationale: The query-param form exists because the browser EventSource API cannot set custom headers. An unset key returns 503 - it fails closed because the feed contains staff PII.

nodes.label: is_working Semantics (open session, overnight aware)
nodes.rationale: A session today with a check_in and no check_out counts; for is_shift_worker employees an open session that started yesterday also counts, because overnight shifts span midnight.

nodes.label: Working-Status Operational Notes (PII, no-store, polling budget)
nodes.norm_label: working-status operational notes (pii, no-store, polling budget)
nodes.rationale: The feed contains personal data (email, phone) so responses are never cached and the key must stay secret. One snapshot is built from a single range query so polling is cheap, but callers should not poll faster than ~once every 10s - use SSE for sub-second freshness. EPF numbers can contain '/' and should be URL-encoded in the epf filter.

nodes.label: Working-Status Snapshot Schema
nodes.rationale: Times are ISO-8601 UTC while calendar dates are Asia/Colombo days; current_session is a convenience mirror of the open session already present in days.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events Snapshot Stream
nodes.rationale: SSE needs a long-running Node host; on short-lived serverless invocations the connection is capped, so callers poll the JSON endpoint instead. The JSON snapshot and the SSE snapshot frame share the exact same shape so a caller can switch freely.

nodes.label: "Working Days" = Days With an Attendance Record
nodes.norm_label: "working days" = days with an attendance record
nodes.rationale: Weekends, holidays and leave days have no attendance record and are therefore skipped, so the 3 prior days returned are the 3 most recent days the person actually worked, looking back up to about three weeks.

nodes.label: Working-Status Route README
nodes.rationale: In-route condensed copy of the public Working-Status contract: auth, modes, snapshot shape and the SSE hosting caveat, kept next to the handler.

nodes.label: Working-Status API (planning-app feed)
nodes.rationale: Real-time feed of who is working right now with each employee's session start/end times for today plus the last 3 working days, designed for server-to-server consumption by the planning app.

nodes.label: AuthProvider onAuthStateChanged Gate
nodes.rationale: _hasHydrated on the auth store only means zustand finished reading localStorage; it says nothing about auth.currentUser. Reading Firestore too early returns permission-denied on a perfectly valid session, so AuthProvider gates on the first onAuthStateChanged callback.

nodes.label: Firestore Rules Are Default-Deny
nodes.rationale: A new collection with no match block has every read and write silently denied; this has caused real bugs more than once.

nodes.label: Fingerprint Firestore Collection Layout
nodes.rationale: attendance_devices, fingerprint_enrollments, fingerprint_attendance_events and fingerprint_last_punch are Admin-SDK-only and denied outright to browsers; attendance_reviews and recalc_queue are readable and transitionable by the web app, and attendance_segments is read-only there.

nodes.label: attendance_segments and recalc_queue
nodes.rationale: Retro-recalculation derives a scheduled vs ot_unverified split into attendance_segments; a roster back-date enqueues recalc_queue work to re-derive those segments.

nodes.label: NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* Keys Are Not Secrets
nodes.rationale: These keys identify the project and do not grant access - Firestore rules do the enforcing - which is why netlify.toml disables Netlify's secret scanner. Every real secret is non-NEXT_PUBLIC_.

nodes.label: Deploy App Before firestore.rules
nodes.rationale: Rules resolve every capability from Firebase Auth custom claims, and only authClaims.ts mints them. A session that has not yet passed through the new AuthProvider carries a token with no capability claims, so tightened rules deny it. Ship the app, let people load it, then push the rules.

nodes.label: tenantRegistry: awaitTenants vs tenantsSync
nodes.rationale: tenantsSync() never blocks and is what adminDbFor uses; awaitTenants() blocks and is what the root layout uses.

nodes.label: tenants.snapshot.json Cold-Start Failsafe
nodes.rationale: Machine-written by npm run tenants:snapshot and never hand-edited; it is the cold-start failsafe and the only list Edge middleware can read.

nodes.label: window.__TENANT__ Injection Ordering
nodes.rationale: The root layout is force-dynamic and resolves the host before any bundle runs; that ordering is load-bearing - it is why module-scope reads like `const F = tenant.features` still work.

nodes.label: adminDbFor(req) in API Routes
nodes.rationale: A bare adminDb() falls back to the env default and will silently read the wrong organisation's data.

nodes.label: Server-Side Tenant Resolution Flow
nodes.rationale: One build serves every domain, so the database cannot come from a build-time env var, and the browser cannot look it up either because it would need the map in order to know which database to open. The server resolves it per request and injects the answer as window.__TENANT__ before any bundle runs.

nodes.label: Snapshot Is a Failsafe, Not a Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: snapshot is a failsafe, not a source of truth
nodes.rationale: Without a shipped snapshot, one bad write or one Firestore outage would leave every domain unable to resolve its own database.

nodes.label: Device Auth: Shared Secret + Registered Device
nodes.norm_label: device auth: shared secret + registered device
nodes.rationale: Replaces Firebase Auth device identity with FINGERPRINT_API_KEY plus a per-device Firestore doc that must be active:true; there is no self-registration, so a terminal is provisioned once by an admin.

nodes.label: External Integration Surfaces
nodes.rationale: Each surface has its own shared secret: FINGERPRINT_API_KEY plus a registered active device for terminals, WORKFORCE_API_KEY for the planning-app feed, ATTENDANCE_JWT_SECRET/EXTERNAL_API_KEY for the Solar app, CRON_SECRET for scheduled jobs.

nodes.label: Fingerprint Attendance API (HF-X05)
nodes.rationale: Adapts the original Firebase Callable Function contract to this app's actual stack: plain Next.js API routes over the same Firestore database as the web app, multi-tenant across altavision.lk and carecode.org.

nodes.label: Admin Device Provisioning Endpoints
nodes.rationale: There is no DELETE - a compromised or decommissioned unit is disabled with PATCH { active: false } so its enrollment and attendance history is kept. workingPlace is the fixed location recorded on every punch because terminals have no GPS, unlike the mobile app.

nodes.label: CLAIMED_CAPABILITIES / claims() Lockstep
nodes.rationale: A claim the rules read but nobody mints reads as false, which is how rule helpers ended up stubbed to isAuth() for months and made every signed-in employee a system admin.

nodes.label: Super Admin (isSuperAdminUser)
nodes.rationale: Granted either by a role capability or the per-user AppUser flag; both resolve through the single definition isSuperAdminUser(). superAdminSync mirrors the account into every tenant database, which is what makes 'every system' true - scope is still 'every system this account exists in', the mirror rather than a standing authority over the deployment.

nodes.label: System Admin (is_system_admin)
nodes.rationale: A capability on a role in ONE tenant's roles collection: full access to that system, ending at that system's border. Most administrators are this and should stay this.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Calendar Hours (Mon-Fri 8h / Sat 4h / Sun rest)
nodes.norm_label: hardcoded calendar hours (mon-fri 8h / sat 4h / sun rest)

nodes.label: work_patterns Model (designed, not built)
nodes.rationale: The attendance calendar hardcodes Mon-Fri=8h, Sat=4h, Sun=rest inside src/app/(pages)/attendance/page.tsx. That is wrong for anyone who rests on a day other than Sunday, works six days, or works shifts - their gauge, their 'Short day' flag and the whole month summary are wrong. The replacement resolves the pattern role -> location -> company -> default.

nodes.label: Attendance Web App README
nodes.rationale: Workforce attendance, leave, scheduling and payroll for several organisations, served by one deployment across several domains: each organisation gets its own Firestore database, branding and enabled modules while sharing one codebase, Firebase project and Auth pool.

nodes.label: Face-Template Backup Extension (SFace)
nodes.rationale: Omitting biometricType still means FINGERPRINT, preserving the metadata-only five-slot contract for existing clients. FACE accepts only portable SFace feature bytes in three slots - never images, thumbnails or Android-Keystore ciphertext - and is deterministic per employee/device so a new enrollment replaces its slots rather than appending.

nodes.label: userId = epf_number Identity Mapping
nodes.rationale: No opaque Firestore auto-id exists here - epf_number is the id used everywhere (attendances, tasks, leaves) and is also the users doc id. employeeId maps to employee_number when present, otherwise falls back to epf_number.

nodes.label: POST/GET /api/fingerprint/enrollments
nodes.rationale: Only enrollment/template metadata is stored - templateDataBase64 for fingerprints is rejected outright (FPA-103) and the endpoint never returns template bytes, so template backup mode from the original contract is not implemented.

nodes.label: POST /api/fingerprint/sync-users
nodes.rationale: Deactivated users are deliberately included so the terminal can disable them locally; nothing is filtered out by `active`. Cursor is nextUpdatedAfter, persisted and passed back as updatedAfter.

nodes.label: --success / --primary / --brand Resolve to One Azure
nodes.rationale: Hue alone cannot distinguish states in this palette - use shape, weight or text instead.

nodes.label: i18n Parity Enforced by TKey
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string needs en + si + ta entries in TRANSLATIONS; the three blocks must hold the same keys in the same order or TKey breaks the build.

nodes.label: Version Bump on Merge / Push Workflow
nodes.norm_label: version bump on merge / push workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires on push to main as well as merged PRs because this project commits straight to main, so a PR-only trigger would never fire. It auto-increments the patch and records a What's New entry; major and minor stay manual.

nodes.label: Serialised Runs and Rebase Before Push
nodes.norm_label: serialised runs and rebase before push
nodes.rationale: A version-bump concurrency group with cancel-in-progress false stops two quick pushes racing on the version files, and `git pull --rebase origin main` before pushing stops the push being rejected as non-fast-forward under rapid direct commits.

nodes.label: Bot Commit Loop Guard
nodes.rationale: The release commit carries [skip ci], which already stops GitHub from re-triggering; the github-actions[bot] author guard is belt-and-braces so the workflow can never loop.

nodes.label: Approval Routing Rules (approvalRouting.ts)
nodes.rationale: A routing rule that can return false for EVERY viewer leaves sessions pending forever and nothing else surfaces them. Shift-place routing did exactly that: a place tagged 'shift' routed only to the employee's assigned supervisor and overrode the place's own supervisor_epfs, so a location supervisor of that place saw nothing to approve. Rules were extracted into a pure, unit-tested module and real data is checked by replaying them with the Admin SDK.

nodes.label: No Overtime Pay in Attendance UI
nodes.norm_label: no overtime pay in attendance ui
nodes.rationale: Labelling extra hours 'Overtime' implies an entitlement that does not exist. The calendar says 'Extra hours'; payroll's PH/Poya multipliers are a separate, genuinely paid concept.

nodes.label: Verification Commands (tsc, node:test, next build --webpack)
nodes.rationale: Plain `next build` FAILS in this repo - the --webpack flag is required. Only one build can run at a time; retry if it reports a lock.

nodes.label: Food-Allowance Flag Computation
nodes.rationale: Computed the same way the Approvals page does (before 06:45 cat 1, 06:45-07:00 cat 2 on check-in, after 19:00 cat 1 on check-out) using Asia/Colombo local time regardless of the server's own timezone.

nodes.label: node:test Over src/lib Pure Logic
nodes.rationale: Tests compile through tsconfig.test.json into .test-out/ and run on node:test with no DOM and no Firestore, so logic worth trusting belongs in src/lib rather than inside a component.

nodes.label: Versioning via src/data/version.json
nodes.rationale: version.json is the single source of truth; patch bumps happen automatically on every merged PR while minor and major are manual.
